results.input: R1 — Price ladder and cosmetic-value expectations: Research verified public pricing, bundle/subscription cosmetic presentation, preview and ownership patterns from game/platform storefronts and official help pages (such as Discord subscription shop profiles and published game storefronts). Identify expectations at free default, mid-included, high-included, £2.99–£4.99 single pack, and £7.99–£12.99 bundle. Include honest-marketing/refund-risk mechanisms from public policies where possible. Output material for T1, T2, and T12.

output.evidence_brief:
**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** Public cosmetic storefront evidence supports a ladder built from distinct access and ownership states rather than gameplay power. Discord presents a free-to-browse catalog available to all users, with preview-and-buy flows for avatar decorations, profile effects, nameplates, and frames; purchased items are described as kept permanently and usable at any time, while the catalog can rotate and limited-time items remain usable after purchase [1](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/17162747936663-Shop-FAQ) [2](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/13410113109911-Avatar-Decorations-FAQ). **VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** Discord also documents subscription-gated value separately: Nitro provides special member pricing, while some exclusive items remain usable only with an active subscription; this is a recurring-access distinction, not permanent ownership [1](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/17162747936663-Shop-FAQ) [2](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/13410113109911-Avatar-Decorations-FAQ).

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** Bundle presentation is explicit: Discord says bundles combine matching or complementary items from a collection at a discount. Its ownership state is visible and consequential: buying one component can mark a bundle “partially owned” and remove eligibility for the bundle discount on the remaining component [1](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/17162747936663-Shop-FAQ) [2](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/13410113109911-Avatar-Decorations-FAQ). **SPECULATIVE TRANSFER.** For SynapticGM, this supports a transparent cosmetic ladder: free default styling; mid-tier included theme elements; high-tier included polish; a £2.99–£4.99 single pack for one clearly previewable accent; and a £7.99–£12.99 bundle for a coherent set of complementary accents. The exact prices are a dossier-design hypothesis, not a verified market average.

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** Storefronts expose price/eligibility states and ownership before or at purchase. Discord documents real-money and Orbs prices on eligible items, member pricing, localized pricing where available, search/filtering, gifting, and prevention of gifting an item already claimed by the recipient [1](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/17162747936663-Shop-FAQ). **SPECULATIVE TRANSFER.** A SynapticGM cosmetic card should show the complete visual result, included components, current ownership, whether the item is permanent or subscription-dependent, and the exact price before checkout; a bundle should show both standalone-equivalent contents and the bundle saving without implying savings after a component has already been bought.

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** Refund rules demonstrate why truthful previews and clear consumption/ownership states matter. Discord states that avatar decorations and profile effects are non-refundable, with case-by-case policy language elsewhere; Epic marks purchases as self-refundable, refundable, or non-refundable and generally excludes consumables, virtual currency, and in-game items; Steam offers defined refund windows for qualifying DLC, bundles, and selected in-game purchases, with consumption, modification, or transfer affecting eligibility; PlayStation limits cancellation after digital download/streaming or delivery of consumables [3](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/360012668071-Refund-Policy) [4](https://legal.epicgames.com/store/refund-policy) [5](https://store.steampowered.com/steam_refunds/) [6](https://www.playstation.com/en-us/legal/playstation-store-cancellation-policy/). **SPECULATIVE TRANSFER.** SynapticGM should put “permanent cosmetic,” “subscription access,” “non-refundable after activation,” and any bundle/partial-ownership restriction beside the purchase action, and should provide an undo/preview state before activation wherever technically possible. These are risk-reduction patterns, not claims that SynapticGM must adopt any particular legal policy.

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** Platform policies also make refunds legible through status labels, usage thresholds, and self-service or support routes: Epic uses refundability labels; Steam publishes timing and usage conditions; PlayStation distinguishes undownloaded add-ons, delivered consumables, bundles, and subscriptions; Discord specifies category-specific exclusions and support channels [3](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/360012668071-Refund-Policy) [4](https://legal.epicgames.com/store/refund-policy) [5](https://store.steampowered.com/steam_refunds/) [6](https://www.playstation.com/en-us/legal/playstation-store-cancellation-policy/). **SPECULATIVE TRANSFER.** A premium theme dossier can treat “honest marketing” as a product feature: use exact component counts, before/after previews, compatibility notes, ownership badges, localized currency when supported, and a direct policy link; never imply that a temporary subscription cosmetic is owned permanently or that a partially owned bundle still grants its original discount. Kits should preserve state semantics and use existing CSS variables / texture and frame tokens, as supplied product law.

output.transfer_patterns:
1. **VERIFIED.** Provide a free default cosmetic state that is complete and legible, then layer premium value through optional decoration rather than reduced usability; Discord’s Shop is available to all users and separates catalog access from Nitro benefits [1](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/17162747936663-Shop-FAQ).
2. **SPECULATIVE.** Use the dossier’s £2.99–£4.99 single-pack band for one tightly scoped, fully previewable accent such as a frame, texture treatment, or motion detail; label the price hypothesis as local product strategy, not a market fact.
3. **SPECULATIVE.** Use the £7.99–£12.99 band for a coherent bundle of matching cosmetics, with the collection relationship and saving shown before purchase; Discord publicly describes matching/complementary discounted bundles [1](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/17162747936663-Shop-FAQ).
4. **VERIFIED.** Show a live or representative preview before purchase; Discord explicitly documents previewing decorations and effects in its Shop and profile flows [1](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/17162747936663-Shop-FAQ) [2](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/13410113109911-Avatar-Decorations-FAQ).
5. **VERIFIED.** Display ownership persistently and distinguish fully owned, partially owned, and unowned states; Discord says partial ownership can remove bundle eligibility [1](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/17162747936663-Shop-FAQ).
6. **VERIFIED.** Separate permanent ownership from subscription-dependent access in copy and badges; Discord says bought decorations remain usable without Nitro, while Nitro-exclusive decorations require an active subscription [2](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/13410113109911-Avatar-Decorations-FAQ).
7. **VERIFIED.** Put exact price options and any member/alternate-currency pricing on the item page or checkout, not only in promotional banners; Discord documents real-money/Orbs presentation, Nitro pricing, and localized-pricing availability [1](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/17162747936663-Shop-FAQ).
8. **VERIFIED.** Use clear refundability or non-refundability labels and explain the trigger that changes eligibility; Epic uses “self-refundable,” “refundable,” and “non-refundable” statuses [4](https://legal.epicgames.com/store/refund-policy).
9. **VERIFIED.** Treat activation, consumption, transfer, and download as distinct events in purchase logic and policy copy; Steam and PlayStation both tie refund eligibility to these states [5](https://store.steampowered.com/steam_refunds/) [6](https://www.playstation.com/en-us/legal/playstation-store-cancellation-policy/).
10. **SPECULATIVE.** Add a pre-activation confirmation that restates the cosmetic contents, permanence, subscription requirement, and refund status, especially for one-click or gift flows; this transfers the transparency logic seen in platform policies without copying their UI or trade dress.
11. **VERIFIED.** Prevent duplicate gifting or visibly explain unclaimed-gift handling; Discord documents that claimed items cannot be gifted and that certain duplicate unclaimed gifts can be returned to the sender [1](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/17162747936663-Shop-FAQ).
12. **SPECULATIVE.** Preserve accessibility by ensuring cosmetics never encode essential status through color, motion, or decorative contrast alone; offer reduced-motion and readable-preview modes while retaining the same cosmetic state semantics and existing CSS variable, texture, and frame tokens.

results.input: R2 — Tabletop/VTT themes, sheets, packs, and previews: Research published public information from D&D Beyond public marketing/help, Fantasy Grounds, Roll20 character sheets/marketplace, Demiplane, Foundry VTT modules/marketplace, and printable premium sheet storefronts. Extract patterns only for paper, hierarchy, frames, modules, previews, typography, and responsive/readable sheet design. No IP copying. Output material for T4 and T7.

output.evidence_brief:
**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** D&D Beyond publicly separates character-sheet decoration into **portrait, frame, backdrop, and theme**, and exposes an **Underdark Mode** that reverses light/dark treatment; the same public help article documents desktop, mobile-browser, and app access, while noting that selected backdrops are not shown on mobile browsers [1](https://www.dndbeyond.com/posts/1003-how-to-customize-your-character-sheet-on-d-d). This is evidence for a layered cosmetic system with explicit cross-device fallback constraints, not evidence about any private implementation.

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** D&D Beyond presents both digital and printable/fillable sheet paths: its public resource page describes tracking core game information in the digital sheet, customizable backgrounds/themes/portraits, downloadable PDFs, fillable PDFs, language variants, and premade sheets [2](https://www.dndbeyond.com/resources/1779-d-d-character-sheets). The transferable lesson is to keep the information architecture stable while allowing surface treatment and print-oriented variants to coexist.

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** Roll20’s public character page positions sheets as system-specific tools that handle rules and math, support in-person play on tablet or laptop, and can export characters into Roll20 games; it reports more than 1,200 supported character sheets [3](https://app.roll20.net/characters). Its public 2024 redesign account describes iterative usability testing, measuring time-on-task and misclicks, collapsing lower-priority information, retaining actions in collapsed panels, and offering card/list views to manage screen real estate [4](https://blog.roll20.net/posts/introducing-the-new-roll20-dungeons-dragons-character-sheet/). These are public product claims and design mechanisms, not competitor-internal data beyond what Roll20 itself published.

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** Foundry’s public package directory distinguishes **Game Systems, Add-on Modules, Game Worlds, Exclusive Content, Premium Content, and Archived Packages**, and separately categorizes **Actor and Item Sheets, Content Packs, Tools and Controls, Visual Effects, and Translation and Localization** [5](https://foundryvtt.com/packages/). The public premium directory shows individual premium entries with package type, compatibility/version, publisher, and purchase links, including theme- and overlay-like modules [6](https://foundryvtt.com/packages/premium). This supports a modular pack model and truthful preview metadata, but does not establish the visual quality or adoption of any listed package.

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** Demiplane’s accessible public shell exposes distinct destinations for **Games, Characters, Homebrew, Campaigns, and Forums** [7](https://app.demiplane.com/home); a public Nexus page separately exposes **Library, Game Rules, Characters, Homebrew, and Campaigns** [8](https://app.demiplane.com/nexus/daggerheart). The evidence supports clear workspace segmentation and direct navigation to character-facing tools; the sparse logged-out shell does not support claims about detailed sheet styling.

**SPECULATIVE TRANSFER.** For SynapticGM, the safest premium direction is a restrained “material system”: paper-like texture, thin frame families, section tabs, and optional surface palettes around unchanged content semantics. Use existing CSS variables plus texture/frame tokens as supplied product law; treat every visual variant as a skin, not a new data model. Avoid protected art, franchise motifs, names, trade dress, and copied UI chrome.

Preserve state semantics and existing CSS variables.
2. **VERIFIED — Offer an accessible dark variant.** Include a deliberate dark-mode treatment with tested text/background contrast rather than merely tinting the light skin; D&D Beyond publicly documents a light/dark reversal mode [1](https://www.dndbeyond.com/posts/1003-how-to-customize-your-character-sheet-on-d-d).
3. **VERIFIED — Design for print and digital together.** Maintain a low-ink, high-contrast printable skin alongside the premium textured skin, reflecting D&D Beyond’s public provision of downloadable and fillable PDFs [2](https://www.dndbeyond.com/resources/1779-d-d-character-sheets).
4. **VERIFIED — Use progressive disclosure.** Collapse secondary details while retaining the primary action or roll affordance in the compact state, as Roll20 publicly describes for skills and other panels [4](https://blog.roll20.net/posts/introducing-the-new-roll20-dungeons-dragons-character-sheet/).
5. **VERIFIED — Provide density modes.** Let users switch between a spacious card presentation and a condensed list presentation for long modules, based on Roll20’s publicly described card/list exploration [4](https://blog.roll20.net/posts/introducing-the-new-roll20-dungeons-dragons-character-sheet/).
6. **VERIFIED — Treat modules as composable packs.** Separate base skin, frame pack, texture pack, sheet accent pack, and optional overlay/module rather than shipping one inseparable theme; Foundry publicly distinguishes systems, modules, worlds, content packs, and visual-effects categories [5](https://foundryvtt.com/packages/).
7. **VERIFIED — Make previews truthful and metadata-rich.** Show compatibility, package type, publisher/creator, and purchase or installation path in previews, matching the public metadata pattern visible in Foundry’s directories [5](https://foundryvtt.com/packages/) [6](https://foundryvtt.com/packages/premium/).
8. **VERIFIED — Use stable section hierarchy across skins.** Keep headings, key values, actions, and editable areas in the same semantic order while changing only paper, borders, accents, and type scale; D&D Beyond publicly describes the sheet as tracking core information while allowing surface styling [2](https://www.dndbeyond.com/resources/1779-d-d-character-sheets/).
9. **VERIFIED — Optimize for tablet and laptop use.** Test premium skins at narrow and wide breakpoints because Roll20 publicly frames character sheets for in-person tablet/laptop play [3](https://app.roll20.net/characters).
10. **VERIFIED — Keep compact controls actionable.** If a panel collapses, leave its most frequent action visible or one tap away; this is directly transferable from Roll20’s documented collapsed skill-check behavior [4](https://blog.roll20.net/posts/introducing-the-new-roll20-dungeons-dragons-character-sheet/).
11. **SPECULATIVE — Use restrained physical-paper cues.** Apply low-frequency fibers, edge wear, ruled dividers, and inset panels at low opacity so they communicate “premium paper” without reducing scanability or resembling a specific game’s art direction.
12. **SPECULATIVE — Build frame families by function.** Offer hairline, dossier, stitched, and archival frame tokens with identical geometry and contrast behavior; vary material impression, not layout or protected trade dress.
13. **SPECULATIVE — Add a preview comparison mode.** Let users toggle “clean / textured / dark / print” in the same sheet viewport and disclose unsupported effects at each breakpoint, extending the cross-device limitation transparency documented by D&D Beyond [1](https://www.dndbeyond.com/posts/1003-how-to-customize-your-character-sheet-on-d-d).
14. **SPECULATIVE — Use typography as hierarchy, not decoration.** Pair one highly legible body face with a restrained display face for titles only; preserve minimum readable sizes, generous line spacing, and numeric alignment in dense stat blocks.
15. **SPECULATIVE — Add a neutral fallback skin.** When a texture, backdrop, or frame is unavailable on a device or print export, fall back to a solid tokenized surface and retain all content/actions; this is a safe product inference from D&D Beyond’s publicly noted mobile backdrop limitation [1](https://www.dndbeyond.com/posts/1003-how-to-customize-your-character-sheet-on-d-d).

results.input: R3 — Trope and material-language competitive patterns: Research public pages or public marketing describing visual skin/theme patterns that overlap with the requested trope clusters: vampire/nocturne, undead/ossuary/bone, dwarf/forge, elf, orc, goblin, merfolk/abyss, cyborg, angelic, infernal, fae, parchment, neon, noir/phosphor/glass. Build an evidence-led catalog of 'done well' visual patterns and recolor/failure risks; make only trope-level, IP-safe transfers. Prioritise Vampire Nocturne vs Undead Ossuary distinction. Output material for T4, T5, T6.

output.evidence_brief:
**Scope and evidence rule.** The reviewed public material is publisher-authored product or design writing, not competitor telemetry. It supports trope-level mechanisms only; it does not justify copying protected characters, names, silhouettes, UI chrome, iconography, or trade dress.

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM — Vampire Nocturne vs. Undead Ossuary.** The strongest verified public contrast in this sample is between *living-night predation* and *post-mortem decay*. The reviewed Blizzard undead page describes Forsaken identity through catacombs, crypts, poisonous sludge, toxic fumes, unlife, and a skeletal horse [1](https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-us/game/races/undead). That is an ossuary/decay language: exposed structure, bone, residue, crypt architecture, and sickly environmental cues. A vampire/nocturne kit should therefore not be treated as a recolor of bone: the **SPECULATIVE TRANSFER** is to use intact, elegant surfaces; restrained blood-red accents; moonlit contrast; shadow, velvet, lacquer, or smoked-glass cues; and a sense of concealment or nocturnal appetite, while reserving bone, cracks, grime, and corpse residue for undead/ossuary.

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM — Forge, dwarf, orc, goblin.** Blizzard’s dwarf page ties the archetype to living stone ancestry, Ironforge, a massive forge, etched stone, warmth, resilience, and heritage armor [2](https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-us/game/races/dwarf). Its orc page uses reinforced construction, spiked metal towers, red-and-black banners, and armored wolves [3](https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-us/game/races/orc). Its goblin page uses mercantilism, explosive inventions, rapid construction, disorder, gambling, and a mechanical trike [4](https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-us/game/races/goblin). These are distinct material directions: **SPECULATIVE TRANSFER** dwarf/forge should emphasize warm iron, hammered planes, rivets, stone grain, and ember-like highlights; orc should emphasize heavy mass, spikes, rugged metal, and high-contrast banners; goblin should emphasize improvised brass, hazard markings, asymmetry, gauges, and playful mechanical clutter. The failure risk is collapsing all three into generic brown metal.

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM — Elf and nature/fae adjacency.** Blizzard’s night-elf page describes elegant bridges, groves, leaf-covered paths, reverence for nature, and a heritage set intended to stand out while blending in with nature [5](https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-us/game/races/night-elf). **SPECULATIVE TRANSFER:** elf/fae cosmetics can differentiate through slender rhythm, botanical filigree, moonlit or bioluminescent accents, and controlled asymmetry rather than simply using green. Avoid direct leaf emblems, named gods, distinctive faction motifs, or recognizable franchise silhouettes.

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM — Cyborg, neon, and readable effects.** Blizzard’s Overwatch design article describes a cyberpunk theme, armor plus color combinations, patterns and textures, multiple weapon/color variations, a customization UI, redesigned VFX, and synth/software-like audio; it also states that special effects were limited to allies because battle scenes already contain substantial visual activity [6](https://overwatch.blizzard.com/en-us/news/23875434/deconstructing-the-cyber-demon-genji-mythic-skin-with-the-overwatch-team/). Riot’s Neon development article describes electricity as the shared power source, speed as the fantasy, and positive/negative charge as a visual/narrative relationship [7](https://playvalorant.com/en-us/news/dev/co-developing-neon-zeri/). **SPECULATIVE TRANSFER:** cyborg/neon should use a small number of emissive channels, modular color variants, crisp edge light, circuit-like linework, and motion/electricity cues; keep silhouettes and state semantics unchanged. The public evidence also supports a photosensitivity/accessibility caution: emissive intensity, flashing, and VFX density need bounded previews and safe defaults.

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM — broader trope separation.** The pages repeatedly make theme legible through coordinated palettes, surface materials, environmental associations, mount/prop cues, and heritage-style sets rather than color alone [1](https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-us/game/races/undead) [2](https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-us/game/races/dwarf) [3](https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-us/game/races/orc) [4](https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-us/game/races/goblin) [5](https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-us/game/races/night-elf). For merfolk/abyss, angelic/infernal, parchment, noir/phosphor, and glass, this review did not find an equally strong official public cosmetic specification; all concrete SynapticGM transfers for those clusters are therefore **SPECULATIVE TRANSFER**, not verified competitor mechanisms. Safe abstractions are water-caustic gradients and shell/pearl gloss for merfolk; halo-like rim light versus ember fissures for angelic/infernal; fibrous warm matte with ink-edge contrast for parchment; near-black surfaces with selective phosphor accents for noir; and translucent, edge-highlighted layers for glass. Do not make any of these cues gameplay-signaling, and do not imply that a transparent or dark theme changes hitboxes, state, rarity, or function.

results.input: R4 — Accessibility and state resilience: Research official WCAG/W3C and MDN guidance on contrast, non-colour semantics, text resizing/reflow, readable type, prefers-reduced-motion, forced colors / contrast, and sound/media controls. Translate to specific, measurable cosmetic-kit acceptance criteria while keeping semantics visible. Output material for T8, T10, and T11.

output.evidence_brief:
**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** W3C WCAG 2.2 is a testable, technology-independent accessibility standard organized around perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust principles; its success criteria are suitable as measurable acceptance requirements ([WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/)).

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** WCAG requires normal text and images of text to reach **4.5:1** contrast, large text to reach **3:1**, and meaningful UI components, state indicators, focus indicators, and graphical objects to reach **3:1** against adjacent colours; ratios are thresholds and must not be rounded ([Contrast Minimum](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum), [Non-text Contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)). Thin strokes can appear weaker in practice, so W3C advises avoiding especially thin shapes or exceeding the threshold.

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** Colour cannot be the only visual means of conveying an action, prompt, distinction, or state. W3C specifically supports adding text, shape, pattern, iconography, or another visible cue; colour coding remains permitted when a non-colour cue is present ([Use of Color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color)).

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** Text must remain usable when resized to **200%** without loss of content or functionality, and non-excepted content must reflow without two-dimensional scrolling at a width equivalent to **320 CSS pixels** for vertically scrolling content ([Resize Text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/resize-text.html), [Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow)). Text-spacing overrides must not break content or controls at line-height **1.5×**, paragraph spacing **2×**, letter spacing **0.12×**, and word spacing **0.16×** the font size ([Text Spacing](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/text-spacing)).

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** MDN documents `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` as a user preference to remove, reduce, or replace non-essential motion; W3C identifies disabling interaction-triggered non-essential animation or offering a user control as sufficient approaches ([MDN prefers-reduced-motion](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/At-rules/@media/prefers-reduced-motion), [Animation from Interactions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions)).

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** In `forced-colors: active`, browsers may replace author colours, remove shadows and non-URL background images, and provide text backplates; MDN advises small targeted adjustments rather than a separate redesign, and notes that native element semantics—not merely added ARIA roles—drive system colour treatment ([MDN forced-colors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/At-rules/@media/forced-colors)).

**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** Automatically playing audio for more than three seconds requires a nearby pause/stop mechanism or independent volume control; W3C discourages autoplay and recommends user-initiated sound ([Audio Control](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-control)). Prerecorded synchronized media with meaningful audio requires synchronized captions, including relevant non-speech sounds, unless it is clearly a text alternative ([Captions Prerecorded](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-prerecorded.html)).

**SPECULATIVE TRANSFER.** For a SynapticGM cosmetic kit, these mechanisms should be applied to cosmetic layers, preview cards, swatches, badges, selected/locked/owned states, animation, and optional sound without changing the product’s supplied law that state semantics remain visible and existing CSS variables plus texture/frame tokens are reused. These are transfer criteria, not claims about any competitor’s implementation or internal data.

1. **VERIFIED.** Set a cosmetic-kit acceptance gate of **≥4.5:1** for normal-size labels, metadata, state text, and text rendered over preview imagery; allow **≥3:1** only for genuinely large text, with the WCAG large-text definition applied consistently.
2. **VERIFIED.** Require every meaningful swatch, badge, border, icon, focus ring, and selected/locked/owned indicator needed to identify a control or state to achieve **≥3:1** against its adjacent colour; do not count nominal ratios that depend on hairline strokes.
3. **VERIFIED.** Preserve state semantics with at least two visible channels: for example, colour plus checkmark, outline/weight change, pattern, text label, or icon. A hue swap alone is a fail for selected, unavailable, warning, or ownership states.
4. **VERIFIED.** Keep the cosmetic preview truthful in monochrome and colour-vision-deficiency review: state meaning must remain recoverable from shape, text, pattern, or iconography without relying on hue recognition.
5. **VERIFIED.** Test the complete kit at **200% text scaling** and reject any clipped, overlapping, obscured, or functionally unreachable title, item name, rarity label, tooltip, button, or state message.
6. **VERIFIED.** Test the cosmetic grid, carousel panels, and detail view at a **320 CSS-pixel equivalent** viewport; non-exempt text and controls must reflow with one-direction reading/interaction, while any intentionally two-dimensional art canvas must retain an accessible textual or structural alternative.
7. **VERIFIED.** Apply the WCAG text-spacing override test at line-height **1.5×**, paragraph spacing **2×**, letter spacing **0.12×**, and word spacing **0.16×**; reject truncation without an explicit reveal mechanism and reject overlap that hides cosmetic names or state semantics.
8. **VERIFIED.** Implement `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` for cosmetic reveals, hover/focus transitions, parallax, shimmer, and carousel movement; replace non-essential movement with an instant state change or a low-motion opacity/colour transition, and provide a persistent motion-off control where animation remains material.
9. **VERIFIED.** Test `forced-colors: active` and ensure selected, focused, locked, and actionable states remain identifiable when gradients, shadows, background textures, and author colours are suppressed; use semantic native controls and targeted system-colour adjustments rather than a wholesale alternate theme.
10. **VERIFIED.** Do not autoplay kit preview audio. If an intentional preview starts sound lasting over three seconds, provide an immediately discoverable pause/stop control and independent volume/mute control; persist the user’s mute choice across cosmetic navigation where the product’s state model permits.
11. **VERIFIED.** For any prerecorded cosmetic showcase video containing meaningful audio, provide synchronized captions covering dialogue and relevant non-speech audio, or clearly label and provide an equivalent text alternative when the media contains no additional information.
12. **SPECULATIVE.** Add an accessibility regression matrix for every cosmetic state × theme surface × preference mode: default, monochrome, `forced-colors: active`, 200% text, 320-CSS-pixel reflow, reduced motion, keyboard focus, and muted audio. This operationalizes the verified mechanisms while preserving existing CSS variables, texture tokens, frame tokens, and visible state semantics.
13. **SPECULATIVE.** Treat decorative texture and frame treatments as progressively removable enhancement: the kit should remain legible and state-complete when texture, shadow, gradient, or animation disappears, while the preview should continue to describe the cosmetic honestly rather than implying effects that accessibility modes suppress.
14. **SPECULATIVE.** Add automated gates for contrast ratios and viewport snapshots, plus manual review for colour-only meaning, forced-colours semantics, reduced-motion behaviour, caption completeness, and truthful previews; automation can detect thresholds but cannot establish that a state is understandable.

results.input: R5 — CSS-safe material and interaction patterns: Research official MDN/web platform/design guidance on CSS gradients, masks, background layers, fonts/font loading, transitions/transforms, performance, and reduced-motion. Develop technically plausible CSS-safe material-language approaches for velvet, bone, soot, brass, parchment, circuit, tide, sulfur, neon, phosphor, glass, and noir. Clearly separate source-backed web capabilities from original SynapticGM recipes. Output material for T3, T6, T9, and T11.

output.evidence_brief:
**VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** CSS gradients are generated images with controllable angles, color stops, hard transitions, repeating variants, and color-interpolation spaces; they can therefore create tunable tonal bands, seams, glints, and grain-like repetition without raster assets ([1](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/gradient/linear-gradient)). **VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** `background-image` accepts comma-separated layers, draws the first layer nearest the user, and supports gradients plus URLs; a solid `background-color` remains an important fallback, while background imagery is not announced by screen readers and must not carry essential meaning ([2](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/background-image)). **VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** `mask-image` accepts generated images such as gradients and multiple mask layers; alpha or luminance determines visibility, so soft fades, cutouts, edge wear, and controlled translucency are feasible, subject to browser compatibility and valid HTTP(S) image sources ([3](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/mask-image)). **VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** `@font-face` defines custom fonts, while `font-display` controls block, swap, fallback, and failure periods; `swap`, `fallback`, or `optional` can preserve readable fallback text during font loading ([4](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/At-rules/@font-face), [5](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/At-rules/@font-face/font-display)). **VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** CSS transitions interpolate changes between states and can be scoped to named properties with duration, delay, and easing rather than applying indiscriminately to `all` ([6](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/transition)). **VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** `transform` supports translate, rotate, scale, skew, and perspective; it creates a stacking context, and MDN specifically advises offering an animation-off control or using `prefers-reduced-motion` for scaling/zooming effects ([7](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/transform)). **VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` detects a user preference to remove, reduce, or replace non-essential motion; large panning and scaling can trigger vestibular discomfort, and a dissolve or opacity alternative is a documented pattern ([8](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/At-rules/@media/prefers-reduced-motion)). **VERIFIED PUBLIC MECHANISM.** Web.dev recommends favoring `transform` and `opacity` for animation, avoiding properties that trigger layout or paint, and using `will-change` sparingly after profiling rather than preemptively ([9](https://web.dev/articles/animations-guide)).

**SPECULATIVE TRANSFER.** SynapticGM can express velvet as a dark base plus low-contrast diagonal/repeating gradients and a restrained moving highlight; bone and parchment can use warm multi-stop gradients with a nearly static paper-fiber overlay; soot/noir can use near-black layered gradients with sparse edge sheen; brass can use narrow warm metallic bands and a masked highlight; circuit can use repeating linear gradients for traces and a mask for clipped routing; tide can use low-amplitude radial/linear layers; sulfur, neon, and phosphor can use a dark base with localized high-luminance accents; glass can use alpha-controlled masks and translucent highlights; these are original recipes, not claims about any competitor or protected visual system. **SPECULATIVE TRANSFER.** Material identity should remain cosmetic: keep text, focus indicators, hit areas, labels, and state semantics unchanged, and route the recipes through the supplied existing CSS variables, texture tokens, and frame tokens. **SPECULATIVE TRANSFER.** A truthful preview should use the same tokenized layers and motion policy as the applied theme, while preserving a readable solid-color fallback and never making a background texture the only carrier of meaning.
